steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (data loss), so I'm stopping before writing anything.

**The consequence:** `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` is irreversible. Per `README.md`, production has 48,000 rows in `users`, and `notes` is a free-text `TEXT` column — whatever is in it is gone the moment the deploy job runs the migration, with no down-migration in this repo (neither existing migration has one) and no way to recover it short of a database restore. "We stopped using it" tells me no code reads it; it doesn't tell me the stored values are worthless.

Two things I need from you before proceeding:

1. **Confirm the drop.** Has anyone checked what's actually in `notes` across those 48,000 rows (e.g. `SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE notes IS NOT NULL AND notes != ''`), and confirmed nothing downstream — exports, reports, support tooling — reads it?
2. **Backup first, or not?** I can make the migration a plain drop as you asked, or have it first copy the data into a `users_notes_archive` table in the same migration so the drop is recoverable. The second is a few extra lines and costs nothing if the column really is empty.

Say go and I'll write `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` as a plain drop and update `schema.sql` to match (it's kept in sync by hand). Tell me which of the two options you want if you'd rather archive first.
I think the app doesn't write to it anymore. Fair, go ahead — plain drop is fine.

Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` (new) — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment-header style of 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the hand-maintained mirror matches the post-migration state.

Not committed (you didn't ask). Nothing run or verified against a database — there's no test setup or SQLite fixture in this repo, so the migration is untested beyond matching the existing files' form. One thing worth knowing before the deploy job picks this up: `DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35 or newer; on anything older the migration will error out rather than silently misbehave.
